intro: Our research is made possible by generous support from national and European funding agencies and foundations.

projects.name: DigiAnaQsim
projects.description: Aims to make quantum simulators more powerful, flexible and useful for understanding complex quantum systems.

projects.name: QUASIMODO
projects.description: QuantERA project studying novel forms of matter using ultracold atoms (dysprosium, potassium, ytterbium) across six European institutions.

projects.name: ISF-DFG Program
projects.description: Joint Israel Science Foundation / DFG grant on sub-wavelength atomic arrays in optical lattices (collaboration with Hebrew University).

projects.name: FOR5919
projects.description: DFG Research Unit on machine-learning applications to complex quantum states, coordinated by the University of Regensburg.

projects.name: FOR5688
projects.description: DFG Research Unit on driven-dissipative quantum systems to engineer low-entropy many-body states.

projects.name: FOR5522
projects.description: DFG Research Unit on out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body physics and thermalization with ultracold atoms.

projects.name: PASQuanS2.1
projects.description: EU Quantum Flagship project developing programmable quantum simulators with enhanced optical-lattice capabilities.

projects.name: DYNAMITE
projects.description: Next-generation quantum simulators for lattice gauge theories.

projects.name: Munich Quantum Valley (TAQC)
projects.description: Trapped-atom quantum computer development using Rydberg states.

projects.name: MCQST
projects.description: Munich Center for Quantum Science and Technology – excellence cluster spanning physics, mathematics, computer science and materials science.

projects.name: FermiQP
projects.description: Hybrid platform combining analogue quantum simulation with digital quantum computing.

projects.name: LaGaTYb
projects.description: ERC project on lattice gauge theories with fermionic ytterbium atoms.

projects.name: FOR2414
projects.description: DFG Research Unit on artificial gauge fields and topological phases in ultracold atoms.
